input.need: cost_per_1k.<arm> prints the per-million-turn cost as if per 1,000: cost_per_1k.brisk-s.few reads "$40.00/1000" while measure.cost_per_1m.brisk-s.few.mean reads "$40.00 per 1,000,000 turns" and cost_per_month.brisk-s.few ($1,200 at 30,000,000 a month) matches the per-million reading. price.*.cost_gap carries the same "/1000" label.
input.why: A reader would take the cost as a thousand times higher than measured.
input.workaround: Cite measure.cost_per_1m.* and cost_per_month.* / price.*.monthly_cost_gap only; never cost_per_1k or price.*.cost_gap.

input.need: What the declared monthly volume (meta.volume_per_month) counts; the input does not name its unit.
input.why: Monthly costs are read at that volume; if it counts conversations rather than routed turns, every monthly figure is off by turns per conversation.
input.workaround: Method says the input does not name the unit and that the monthly figures read it as turns, the unit the cost is priced in.

doc.headline: Use {arm:brisk-s.few} for the turn router: of the {n_candidates|words} configurations it is the only one inside every gate, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.few|usd_whole} a month.
doc.lede: It clears balanced accuracy by {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap|pts} points and its weakest cell, Complex × News, by {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.gap|pts} points, both beyond their intervals. The call moves only if its p95 latency, read without an interval, proves slower in production, or if the cell floor were lowered enough to admit the cheaper {arm:nano-xs.few}.

Only if a fresh run reads Brisk-S few-shot's balanced accuracy more than {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap|pts} points lower than today. decision.text: Ship {arm:brisk-s.few} on all turns. Balanced accuracy is {measure.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.mean} ({overall_interval.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.interval|interval}, derived), every cell holds its floor and p95 latency is {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.few.p95}.

{arm:nano-xs.few} would cost {cost_per_month.nano-xs.few|usd_whole} a month but misses the floor in Complex × News at {criteria.cell_floor.nano-xs.few.complex.news.value}, clear of its interval. {arm:atlas-m.few}, {arm:atlas-m.rubric} and {arm:brisk-s.rubric} are more accurate but blow the {criteria.p95.threshold} latency budget. The rest miss the accuracy gate.

The weakest margin is {weakest.arm} on {weakest.criterion}: {weakest.value} against {weakest.threshold}, {weakest.margin|pts} points. method.text: Each configuration labelled {scoreboard.brisk-s.few.cases|int} turns once, none lost; the matrix crosses complexity (Simple, Medium, Complex) with domain (Science, Conversational, News), and each cell holds the same count for every configuration.
A turn is correct when the predicted complexity and domain label matches the gold label. Accuracy is read per cell; balanced accuracy is the plain mean of the cells.

Cell accuracy carries a stated 95% half-width. Balanced accuracy's interval is derived from its cells (the root of their squared standard errors over their count), so it is called derived. Comparisons between configurations are unpaired and uncorrected for multiplicity.

Declared before the run: balanced accuracy at least {criteria.overall.threshold}, accuracy at least {criteria.cell_floor.threshold} in every cell, p95 latency at most {criteria.p95.threshold}. A figure on the passing side whose interval crosses its line passes and is called borderline.
One p95 per configuration, stated with no interval and no count of the requests behind it.
Measured cost per million routed turns. Monthly figures read the declared volume of {meta.volume_per_month} a month; the input does not say what that volume counts, and it is read here as turns.
There is no production router or control, and no mix of configurations by cell was run.

content.text:
I recommend shipping Brisk-S few-shot. Of the nine configurations, it is the only one that passes all three gates (balanced accuracy, the 80% floor in every cell, and the 250 ms p95 latency budget). The draft passed the final pre-submission check with no faults, and the editor hasn't seen it yet. I made one small wording change in Method after that check ("Declared before the run" now reads "None was set after the results"), so it hasn't been rechecked.

- **The deciding finding:** Brisk-S few-shot clears balanced accuracy by 0.7 points and its weakest cell (Complex × News) by 2.9 points. Both clearances sit outside their intervals.
- **The main risk:** its p95 latency (184 ms, against the 250 ms budget) is a single figure with no interval. If its true p95 is more than 66 ms higher in production, no configuration passes. The first next step is to measure p95 on production traffic, in parallel with shipping.
- **The tempting alternative:** Nano-XS few-shot would save about $1,143 a month. It is level with or ahead of Brisk-S in most cells, but falls 6.2 points behind in Complex × News (76.7%), clearly below the floor. It is priced in the report only as a labelled what-if.
- **The more accurate options:** the Atlas-M few-shot, Atlas-M rubric and Brisk-S rubric configurations all fail on latency alone.

I logged two problems along the way:
- **Cost labels:** the "cost per 1,000" figures print the per-million cost as if it were per 1,000, which makes them look a thousand times too high. The report uses only the per-million and monthly figures.
- **Monthly volume:** the input doesn't say what its 30 million a month counts. Method says the report reads it as turns, the unit cost is priced in.
